title: Resilience Scenario Classifier and Mitigation Library
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This page defines a compact taxonomy of platform resilience scenarios relevant to LLM inference, maps each to observable signals and dashboards, and provides a curated mitigation library (playbook snippets, severity mappings, and ownership). The goal is to reduce operator decision time by standardizing classification, automating initial containment, and surfacing the correct runbook quickly.

Audience:
- Platform operators
- Oncall SREs
- Runtime and infra engineers
- Incident commanders

Scope:
Covers multitenant inference runtime, GPU pools, KV/prefix cache, model variant routing, and control-plane routing. Does NOT replace individual service runbooks; instead it is a classification-and-routing layer to pick the right runbook and initial actions.

Classification: quick reference (operator-facing)
1) Capacity Saturation (Tier: Service / Severity: P2–P1)
   - Definition: Sustained queue depth or resource utilization above safe thresholds causing tail latency SLO burn and dropped requests.
   - Key signals: queue_depth > 1200 across pool, 95th CPU/GPU util > 92%, sustained SLO error rate > 5% for 10+ minutes.
   - PromQL examples:
     - sum(queue_depth) by (pool) > 1200
     - histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 1.2
   - Primary dashboards: "Capacity Heatmap", "Tail-latency by tenant"
   - First responders: capacity-allocator oncall, platform-operator

2) Cache Degradation (Tier: Storage-Adjacent / Severity: P2–P3)
   - Definition: High miss rates or KV prefix cache inconsistencies causing repeated model recomputation and token cost spikes.
   - Key signals: cache_miss_rate > 30% for 5m, increased token-per-request metric +20%.
   - Observation queries:
     - rate(kv_cache_misses[5m]) / rate(kv_cache_requests[5m]) > 0.3
   - Impact: cost increase, higher average latency, potentially cold-start cascades.

3) Model Variant Mismatch or Misrouting (Tier: Serving / Severity: P1–P2)
   - Definition: Requests routed to incompatible or non-optimized model variants (e.g., quantized mismatch) causing inference errors or timeouts.
   - Key signals: model_error_rate > 1% for a given variant, model-version-mismatch alerts, sudden increase in function-call retries.

4) External Dependency Failure (Tier: External Integrations / Severity: P1–P3)
   - Definition: Failure of external systems (storage, upstream auth, telemetry backend) that degrades platform capability.
   - Signals: downstream_5xx_count > baseline, auth_latencies spike, telemetry write failures.

5) Regional Degradation / Network Partition (Tier: Network / Severity: P1)
   - Definition: Partial regional loss or high inter-region latency causing routing fallbacks and regional SLO divergence.
   - Signals: region_request_loss_rate > 2%, cross-region RTT > 200ms, region-specific capacity alarms.

6) Regression / Model Quality Drop (Tier: Product / Severity: P2)
   - Definition: Automatic quality monitors report regression against benchmark prompt-sets leading to customer-visible accuracy regressions.
   - Signals: eval_suite_failure_rate, CR/QA alerts, user-reported quality incidents.

Mitigation Library (playbook snippets)
For each scenario, the following snippets are intended to be copy-pasteable into incident channels. They are ordered: immediate containment -> targeted mitigation -> remediation -> post-incident actions.

Capacity Saturation (Immediate containment)
1. Set temporary tenant throttles: run `rctl tenant throttle --tenant $TENANT --qps 0.5` for the top 3 noisy tenants (operator-approved).
2. Invoke pre-warm: `infractl gpu warmup --pool $POOL --target 15` to bring minimal warmset.
3. If tail-latency continues, initiate routing shed: change routing policy to `degradation-mode:cautious` via the console API.

Capacity Saturation (Targeted mitigation)
1. Toggle canary to lower-cost model variant for non-critical tenants: `apictl route update --route /v1/generate --model small-qa:v2 --filter tenant:non-critical`.
2. Increase burst credits for critical tenants for 15 minutes.

Cache Degradation (Immediate containment)
1. Rehydrate hot prefixes: `cache-ops rehydrate --prefixes-file /tmp/hot_prefixes.txt` (see appendix for generation).
2. Temporarily increase cache eviction threshold to favor prefixes older than 20 min.

Cache Degradation (Targeted mitigation)
1. Run prefix-hit rehearsal job: `jobs/run_prefix_rehearsal --window 30m --sample 5%`.
2. If inconsistent KV reads detected, create read-fallback: `kv-proxy set fallback_read true` and route KV reads to consistent backends.

Model Variant Mismatch (Immediate containment)
1. Pin routing policy to last-known-good model: `routingctl pin --route /v1/chat --model $MODEL_ID --duration 30m`.
2. Disable JIT kernel switching for affected hosts: `hostctl feature disable jit-kernel`.

Regional Degradation (Immediate containment)
1. Flip region routing to global fallback: `route-policy apply --policy regional-fallback`.
2. Notify oncall to prepare cross-region capacity transfers; allocate warm spare instances.

Severity mapping and escalation rules
- P1 (Critical): Regional outage, persistent P99 tail latency > SLO for >15 minutes, or major dependency failure. Pager to oncall + incident lead, notify C-level if >60 minutes.
- P2 (High): Localized capacity issues, model-routing problems with measurable user impact. Pager to oncall, Slack channel escalation to platform team.
- P3 (Medium): Degraded telemetry, transient cache misses, or minor degradations. Alert to queue for next business-day or oncall depending on recurrence.

Playbook decision matrix (simplified)
Columns: Impacted Tenants | Severity | Initial Action | Can Auto-Contain?
- Customer-critical only | P2 | Pin model or increase credits | Yes (automated)
- Multitenant noisy | P1 | Throttle noisy tenants + shed | Partial
- All regions | P1 | Trigger regional fallback + incident | No

Dashboards and alerting guidance
- Panels recommended for the operator home screen:
  - Multitenant SLO synthesis (per-tenant P50/P95/P99, burn rates)
  - Capacity heatmap (pool-level GPU utilization, queue depth)
  - KV-prefix hit/miss ratio trend
  - Model-variant error rate by version
  - Cross-region latency and dropped-route counts

- Alert design templates (examples):
  - Alert: "pool_high_queue_depth"
    - Expr: sum(queue_depth{pool="$POOL"}) > 1200
    - For: 10m
    - Severity: P1
    - Runbook: link to this page + capacity-saturation-runbook
\  - Alert: "kv_cache_miss_spike"
    - Expr: increase(rate(kv_cache_misses[5m]) / rate(kv_cache_requests[5m]), 5m) > 0.15
    - For: 5m
    - Severity: P2

Operational automation recommendations (safe defaults)
1. Auto-throttle noisy tenants when their token-per-second exceeds 3x baseline for >3m.
2. Automated rehydrate job triggered when cache_miss_rate > 25% for 10m.
3. Automated warmup when queue depth > 800 for 5m and predicted demand (ML model) > 1.2x baseline.

Ownership and contact matrix
- capacity-allocator (primary) — oncall rotation: capacity-allocator@pagerduty 
- platform-operator (secondary) — oncall rotation: platform-operator@pagerduty
- runtime-team — responsible for model routing and variant pinning
- infra-storage — KV/prefix cache ownership

Rollback and remediation criteria (decision checkpoints)
1. Rollback a mitigation (e.g., throttle) when SLO burn rate <1% for 30m and queue_depth trending down for two consecutive 5m windows.
2. Do not rollback until postmortem owner assigned and action items created if incident lasted >30m.

Post-incident playbook & retrospective triggers
- Minimum post-incident items to file within 72 hours:
  1. Short incident timeline (5–10 bullets)
  2. Root cause hypothesis and supporting telemetry snippets
  3. Action owner and ETA for each action
  4. Validated rollback and gating criteria for future rollouts
- Automatic retrospective trigger when incident exceeds 60 minutes or P1 severity.

Appendix: useful CLI references and sample PromQL queries
- Rehydrate generation: `python tools/hot_prefix_extractor.py --window 15m --out /tmp/hot_prefixes.txt`
- Sample PromQL list:
  - queue_depth by pool: sum(queue_depth) by (pool)
  - kv miss ratio: sum(rate(kv_cache_misses[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests[5m]))
  - model error rate: sum(rate(model_errors_total[5m])) by (model_version) / sum(rate(model_requests_total[5m])) by (model_version)

Appendix: dashboard panel YAML example (for dashboards-as-code)
- name: Pool capacity heatmap
  expr: sum(queue_depth) by (pool)
  type: heatmap
  thresholds: "[0, 400, 800, 1200]"
